name: Sacar
overview: Sacar was a male member of the tribe of Levi, distinguished as the fourth-born son of Obed-edom. His identity is primarily defined by his lineage within the Levitical family, which was significant for service in the house of the Lord. Beyond his birth order and tribal affiliation, Scripture provides no additional details about his life or role.
namesAndTitles: The name Sacar means "reward [given by G-d]" or possibly "hired hand," reflecting a name of Hebrew origin that may indicate a role or blessing associated with his identity. This proper name was not given directly by God but appears in the biblical record as such.
familyAndRelationships: Sacar is explicitly identified as the son of Obed-edom, situating him within a notable Levitical family. Scripture does not record any further family relationships beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Sacar's significance in Scripture is tied to his position within the Levitical lineage, specifically as a descendant of Obed-edom, who was entrusted with responsibilities related to the house of the Lord. While Sacar himself is not described as performing specific acts, his inclusion in the genealogical record underscores the importance of faithful Levitical service in the worship and maintenance of God's sanctuary.
